findings.title: Date override match skips busy-time check
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, once any date override is found for the slot's calendar day and the slot is treated as inside that override, the function returns true immediately. It never runs the busy-interval check below. Fixed hosts (and round-robin hosts) with a date override can therefore be offered slots that overlap existing bookings or calendar busy times, so the booking page will show times that cannot actually be booked.

findings.title: All-day block override never matches
findings.body: A blocked day is detected with `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)`. Dayjs instances are compared by object identity, so this is always false even when the instants are equal. The callback then fails to reject the slot, dateOverrideExist is set, and the following branch returns true. An override whose start equals its end (the usual "unavailable all day" marker) makes the fixed host look fully available that day instead of blocked.

findings.title: Multiple overrides are treated as an intersection
findings.body: dateOverrides.find returns the first override for which the callback returns true, and the callback returns true when the slot is merely outside that one window (before its start or after its end). If a host has two override ranges on the same day, a slot inside the second range is still outside the first, so find succeeds and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. Only a slot that sits inside every override at once survives. Split date overrides (for example morning and afternoon) disappear from round-robin availability.

findings.title: Working-hours fallback allows non-working days
findings.body: When no date override applies, availability is rejected only if workingHours.find returns a row whose days include the slot's UTC weekday and whose range does not contain the slot. If the fixed host simply does not work that weekday, no row matches, find returns undefined, and the function falls through to the busy check and returns available. Round-robin slots generated from other hosts are therefore still bookable on days the fixed host has no working hours. The end bound is also wrong: both start and end are computed from slotStartTime, so a slot that starts inside hours but runs past endTime is not rejected, and those minute values are UTC while WorkingHours may be organizer-local minutes.

findings.title: Override timezone shift wraps and can throw
findings.body: The new override window is built with dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone). timeZone is optional on TimeRange; if a caller omits it, tz(undefined) throws and slot generation fails. Date.toString() is a locale string, so the parsed instant (and thus the DST offset) is unreliable. The shifted time is then reduced with .hour() and .minute() only, so an offset that crosses midnight wraps to the same invitee day (23:00 plus two hours becomes 01:00, or a negative offset becomes a late evening). buildSlots also drops ranges where start >= end, so a wrapped override window produces no slots or slots on the wrong day.
